clue.text: Fresh backing to port in Buckinghamshire

indicators.note: something backing goes in reverse, so the word before it is read from its end

parts.note: fresh means new
Dover is the Channel port in Kent

explanation.surface: Someone pushing a fresh scheme to develop a port somewhere inland in Buckinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Buckinghamshire is a county north-west of London; WENDOVER is a small market town there, well away from any sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Wendover is a market town lying in the Chiltern Hills of that English county.

clue.text: So many round holes

parts.note: surface reading: a large number of circular openings; setter's reading: a round of golf, and how many holes it has

explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a shape, but it is the golfing noun: a standard round of golf is played over that many holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A full golf course and a standard round of the game both consist of this number of holes.

clue.text: Is nobleman in trade, possibly? Familiar figure in the City

indicators.note: in places the first words inside the letters of what follows
possibly signals that the word could be arranged some other way

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman
taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether an aristocrat has gone into business, then a well-known face in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the square mile of London that houses its banks and financial markets, so the figure is a number, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The rate at which a central bank lends to banks is a number constantly watched by London financiers.

clue.text: Accommodation for  leading service-man

parts.note: surface reading: housing for a senior member of the armed forces; setter's reading: the man who leads a church service, and his house

explanation.walkthrough: 'Service-man' suggests a soldier or sailor; here the service is a church one, and the man leading it is the parish priest.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the house provided by the parish for the clergyman who conducts its church services.

clue.text: Transmit the aria Ted composed

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are assembled into something new

parts.note: the words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A radio station broadcasting a song that a man called Ted wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: To send out signals or energy in all directions is to give them off, or broadcast them.

clue.text: Worry, upset about one's profession

parts.note: worry and care are both anxiety

indicators.note: a down clue's word upset is turned over, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone fretting and distressed about the job they do.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's chosen occupation, followed through working life, is their line of work.

clue.text: How to reach airport — or the end of the runway?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hired car carrying a passenger

definitions.note: the movement an aircraft makes there, rather than a place
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what an aircraft does along the ground before and after flying

explanation.surface: A traveller wondering how to get to the airport, or where the plane will stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a cab you hire, and also the verb for an aircraft moving slowly on the ground.

clue.text: It could be time to define this clue

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a prison term handed down by a judge
second meaning: a grammatical unit of words like the one you are reading

explanation.surface: A setter musing that the moment has come to pin down what this clue means.
explanation.walkthrough: Doing time is serving a prison term; the clue itself is a complete grammatical unit of words.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a punishment imposed by a court and a complete group of words with a verb.

clue.text: Water from the Eden river?

parts.note: surface reading: water taken from the River Eden in Cumbria; setter's reading: the Garden of Eden, so the drink of its first man

explanation.walkthrough: The Eden is a real river in north-west England, but the clue means the biblical garden; the phrase is an old jocular name for plain water.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain drinking water is humorously named after the first man, who had nothing stronger to drink.

clue.text: The seven acts of Jacques

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a play's divisions, or seven deeds of a man
setter's reading: Jaques's speech in As You Like It, where a man's life is a play of seven periods

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's As You Like It, Jaques says all the world's a stage, and one man in his time plays many parts, 'his acts being seven' stages of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaques describes a man's life as seven periods, from infant to second childhood, each one a stage of life.

clue.text: Musician gets wine to carry in — it's distributed by the leader

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the wine surrounds the next piece

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
taken as written

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: An orchestral player is given wine, which the orchestra's leader hands round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The leader' sounds like the leader of an orchestra, but it means only the first letter of the.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the clarinet, a woodwind instrument, is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Where skippers first got to know the ropes?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: children with skipping ropes learning how to jump
setter's reading: ship's captains learning seamanship on a vessel used for instruction

explanation.walkthrough: Skippers suggests children skipping with ropes; a skipper is also a ship's captain, and knowing the ropes is learning a sailor's trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel used to teach young sailors seamanship is where future captains learned their trade.

clue.text: The ugly sister who turned to sculpture?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: one of Cinderella's ugly sisters taking up carving
setter's reading: a hideous sister of myth whose gaze turned people into stone statues

explanation.walkthrough: Ugly sister calls up Cinderella's pantomime sisters; the setter means the Gorgons, three monstrous sisters of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: She was one of the three Gorgon sisters, snake-haired and so hideous that her look petrified onlookers.

clue.text: Herb and Jack continue to tease

parts.note: jack and tar are both old words for a sailor
to rag someone is to tease them
to carry on is to continue

explanation.surface: A man called Herb and his friend Jack keep teasing each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Herb and Jack look like two men's names; the first is the definition. Rag on, meaning keep teasing, reads in the order tease, continue.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic plant, used in French cooking and in flavoured vinegar, is a culinary herb.

clue.text: A second heart? No trouble

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, and disturbed letters lose their order

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A patient told about a second heart, and assured it will be no trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A second heart' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at A second.
explanation.definitionFit: One more of the same kind, an additional one, is a second of something.

clue.text: Proverbially nothing but variety in flavouring

parts.note: nothing but means all, as in all talk
the proverb calls variety the spice of life
points to the saying variety is the spice of life

explanation.surface: A cook relying on the saying that variety is everything when seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: This spice, the dried berry of a West Indian tree, is a widely used food seasoning.

clue.text: Cheat is a bestial person — holds back 550

indicators.note: holds means keeps inside, so the person surrounds the number

parts.note: a swine is a brutish, contemptible person

indicators.note: back says the number's letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: in Roman numerals L is 50 and D is 500

explanation.surface: Calling a cheat a beast who keeps back 550 pounds of someone's money.
explanation.definitionFit: To trick someone out of their money is to defraud or cheat them.

clue.text: Implicated wanting a definition of "prodigal"?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: someone involved in a lack, a need for something
setter's reading: the dictionary sense of prodigal, recklessly spendthrift

explanation.walkthrough: The prodigal son of the parable squandered his inheritance; the adjective prodigal means spending recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal describes someone who squanders money and resources extravagantly, and the answer is its everyday synonym.

clue.text: Tear material, then repair tear

parts.note: lace is an openwork fabric

indicators.note: to repair is to rework something, so the letters are put back together differently

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for ripping fabric and then mending the rip.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate flesh or skin is to rip or gash it roughly.

clue.text: Theatre assistant could be Welsh?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the person who helps an actor into costume

definitions.note: an example of the furniture, not the word itself
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a Welsh ..., a kitchen sideboard with shelves for plates

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a backstage helper comes from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: A Welsh dresser is a tall wooden kitchen cupboard with open plate shelves above.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a backstage helper with costumes and a piece of kitchen furniture, as in Welsh dresser.

clue.text: A blow for a Syrian, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a strong easterly wind in the western Mediterranean
second meaning: a native of the Levant, the eastern Mediterranean coast

explanation.surface: Someone from Syria suffering a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A blow' suggests a misfortune, but it is a wind; the Levant includes Syria, Lebanon and Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an easterly Mediterranean wind and also a person from the eastern Mediterranean lands, which include Syria.

clue.text: A way fruit is raised in an Arctic region

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted up, so the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
a nut is a hard-shelled fruit

explanation.surface: A method of growing fruit in the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: The treeless, frozen plains of the far north, with permanently frozen subsoil, form a polar landscape.

clue.text: Scene-shifter meets a Roman philosopher

indicators.note: a shifter moves things about, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stagehand bumps into an ancient Roman thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scene-shifter' reads as a stagehand who moves scenery; split, it is the word and its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca the Younger was a Stoic thinker and tutor to the emperor Nero in first-century Rome.

clue.text: Prayers for fishermen?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: recitations of the Lord's Prayer in Latin

definitions.note: describes the tackle by its users; the answer names the lines themselves
definitions.meaning: second meaning: fishing lines with hooks spaced along them like rosary beads

explanation.surface: Wondering which prayers are said on behalf of men at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lord's Prayer in Latin begins Our Father; anglers use the same name for a weighted line carrying several hooks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means recitations of the Lord's Prayer and also anglers' multi-hook tackle, so both senses fit.

clue.text: As nurses are so liable to do

definitions.meaning: surface reading: something nurses are inclined to do
setter's reading: the word means both look after patients and be inclined

explanation.walkthrough: Nurses look after the sick, and the same short verb also means be inclined or likely, as in 'liable to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurses care for patients, and being liable or inclined towards something is the other sense of the verb.

clue.text: Chief part for Anthea, doubtless

indicators.note: a part of the following words is all that is wanted, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Anthea is certain to get the leading role in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief part' sounds like a lead role in a play, but chief is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief is a leader or person in charge, such as the principal of a school.

clue.text: Talk with many about poetry

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, a large number
on means about, as in a talk on art
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Discussing poems with a crowd of people.
explanation.walkthrough: Many as C, the Roman hundred, is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to hold a conversation, chatting with someone.

clue.text: Sinks again as the river goes by

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
time elapses when it goes by

explanation.surface: Something keeps going under while the river flows past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinks' suggests going under water, but here it is falling back into illness or bad habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who relapses slips back into a worse condition, declining once more after improving.
